title: Your memories shouldn’t need a form.
text: Your memories shouldn’t need a form. OpenMemory turns a simple thought into something you can return to.

title: A book you want to read.
text: First, a book. I want to read Sapiens. That’s an intention, not a finished book. The subject and the action both matter.

title: Fine-tuned locally.
text: On this Mac, a fine-tuned model classifies the note using M L X. A separate local model extracts the details. These are actual app captures, with processing waits shortened.

title: Review before you keep it.
text: The review shows Book, Sapiens, and something I want to do. Check it, edit it, and confirm. Nothing is saved before you say so.

title: And a movie you loved.
text: Now a movie. I watched Arrival and loved it. The model recognizes a movie, but leaves the action uncertain. Review lets you choose what happened before saving.

title: Your story, together.
text: The book stays on your wishlist. The movie becomes a watched film you loved, after confirmation. Both are saved in this browser, and survive a reload.

title: A real experiment. Honest results.
text: The adapter trained on seven hundred and thirty examples. In a two hundred note test, joint accuracy rose from sixty-seven to seventy-six point five percent, still below the eighty-one percent majority baseline. It remains experimental.

title: AI suggests. You decide.
text: Explore the app, research code, and published model. OpenMemory. A I suggests. You decide what becomes a memory.
